scenario: AITA for catching my parents disputes on a video conference when I'm working from home? | I am in my early 20s and I have a full time job. I'm living at home right now because, right when cuarantine was starting, I tried to renew my apartment lease and my landlord refused me, saying he was selling the building for condos. So with all the shutdowns, I wasn't able to find a new apartment in time and my parents let me move back in. It's really not ideal and I've actually signed a new apartment lease that starts in a month. I wish it was sooner but housing near me is very competitive. My parents have always had a very disfunctional relationship. But they won't leave each other. No matter how much drama they have, I think they've lived like this too long to consider anything else. I have my work setup in the formal dining room which is rarely used. The room opens to the main entry hallway, and there is no door there. So there's less privacy than I'd prefer. I was hosting a meeting this morning and several of my coworkers were attending. First, unfortunately, that kind of thing has been really normalized for me, it doesn't register as a big deal. I said yeah, this shit was normal for all my life, I was just annoyed at the timing but I wasn't scared or some shit. My other co-workers trickled back in. My parents were still going hog wild in the hallway, and I eventually said "hey could yall keep it down, I'm presenting for a meeting." My dad saw that they were on camera first, and got really mad at me. Yelling at me to get the fuck out of his house. I went out to my car and took my laptop and finished the meeting in there. But when I came back in my parents were both over yelling at each other for the moment and they were both furious at me for "filming a private family matter for everyone to see" and shit like that. I said that I wasn't trying to film them, I was on camera myself because I was doing a presentation and they walked right in and started screaming. And if they'd stopped to think or look around at all they'd see I was trying to work quietly. My parents kicked me out and I'm at a hotel now. My parents want an apology and I don't know what to do. I think I might to keep the peace but I don't really feel bad for what I did. AITA for getting my parents argument on a video conference?
